assertion: Three years ago, U.S. utilities expected peak electricity demand to grow by about 24 gigawatts over the following five years. Their most recent forecasts put that figure at roughly 166 gigawatts, 6.9 times the earlier estimate, and about 90 gigawatts of the increase is tied to data centers.
independent_value: Grid Strategies 2025 national load growth report: 24 GW -> 166 GW (6.9x), ~90 GW data centers

sources.title: Grid Strategies National Load Growth Report 2025

assertion: Data centers used about 4.4% of U.S. electricity in 2023, according to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and the lab projects that share could reach 6.7% to 12% by 2028.
the average U.S. residential price rising from 17.3 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2025 to 18.2 cents in 2026
warehouse_value: 2025 residential US avg 17.3 c/kWh (2024: 16.48); current STEO shows 17.2 for 2025, a rounding/vintage difference
sql: SELECT price_year, avg_price_cents_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr='US' AND sector_code='RES' AND price_year IN (2024,2025)

assertion: expects record national electricity sales in 2026, driven by data center development and manufacturing
source_finding: EIA STEO attributes record 2026 sales to commercial (data center) and industrial demand growth
independent_value: EIA STEO electricity section

assertion: Researchers at the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas estimate that existing data centers have already raised wholesale electricity prices by 2% to 6% on average nationwide.
independent_value: Dallas Fed WP 2606: 2-6% wholesale effect (a modeled estimate)

assertion: wholesale power typically makes up about half of the retail price of electricity
independent_value: Dallas Fed commentary

assertion: a given increase in wholesale prices reaches retail bills at roughly half its size
source_finding: Dallas Fed commentary states roughly half pass-through
independent_value: Dallas Fed commentary

assertion: Its clearing price rose from $28.92 per megawatt-day for 2024/2025 to $269.92 for 2025/2026, then hit a federally approved cap in each of the next three auctions. The 2028/2029 auction cleared at $325 per megawatt-day and still came in 6,831 megawatts short of PJM's reliability requirement.
sql: SELECT delivery_year, resource_clearing_price FROM energy.pjm_capacity_auction_prices WHERE lda='RTO' AND delivery_year>=2024

assertion: PJM's independent market monitor attributes about 46% of capacity costs across the last four auctions, or $29.4 billion, to data center demand.
independent_value: IMM (Bowring) via Utility Dive: ~46%, $29.4B. A monitor attribution, contested by others.

assertion: The Midcontinent grid operator saw summer capacity prices reach a record $666.50 per megawatt-day for 2025/2026 as its surplus shrank. A year later, the picture shifted. Capacity offered into the 2026/2027 auction grew 3.4%, led by solar additions, and annualized prices fell to between $116 and $126 per megawatt-day, down from $212 to $217 the year before.
independent_value: MISO PRA presentation and Utility Dive match

assertion: In August 2026, Gov. Greg Abbott directed state regulators and ERCOT to audit every data center seeking a grid connection before any project moves forward, citing more than 474 gigawatts of requests, more than five times the state's record peak demand, with about 90% coming from data centers.
independent_value: Texas governor release matches

assertion: Georgia Power's pipeline of prospective large-load projects grew from about 16,000 megawatts in 2023 to roughly 69,000 megawatts by December 2025, about 80% of it from data centers.
independent_value: Atlanta News First / PSC chair reporting matches

assertion: Georgia Power projects that new large-load contracts will produce about $950 million a year in customer savings beginning in 2029
independent_value: Georgia Power Aug 26 2026 release: approximately $950 million per year beginning 2029 (a company projection)

sources.title: Georgia Power release via PR Newswire/Placera

assertion: state commission staff cautioned that the related generation buildout could add around $20 a month to residential bills
independent_value: Atlanta News First: PSC staff cautioned it could add $20 a month; a later stipulation guaranteeing 2029-31 revenue means, per Georgia Power, the increase will not materialize (omitted by the article)

assertion: Data centers account for roughly 15% of the current load of Oregon's investor-owned utilities, according to the state's utility commission. Under a 2025 state law, Oregon regulators approved new rates for Portland General Electric in July 2026 that raised data center rates by an average of 29% while lowering residential rates by 1.3% and commercial rates by 2.1%.
independent_value: Oregon PUC report pp.2,8: roughly 15 percent of IOU load; PUC release PR-26-15: 29% increase, residential -1.3%, commercial -2.1%

assertion: North Dakota saw electricity demand grow almost 40% while inflation-adjusted prices fell by about 3 cents per kilowatt-hour.
reason: Figure comes from a Boston Globe/LBNL analysis with an unstated window and was not re-derived. Warehouse ND all-sector sales rose 18.5 to 30.3 TWh (+64%) 2016-2025 and 22.9 TWh in 2021 (+24% from 2016), while nominal price fell only 8.94 to 8.20 c/kWh; the article's window is unknown.
searched: North Dakota electricity demand 40% inflation-adjusted prices fell 3 cents Boston Globe
LBNL retail electricity price trends North Dakota
measure: North Dakota electricity sales and price
sql: SELECT price_year, avg_price_cents_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr='ND' AND sector_code='ALL'

assertion: Utility forecasts add up to about 90 gigawatts of new data center load by 2030, while data center market analysts estimate growth is unlikely to need much more than 65 gigawatts over that period.
independent_value: Grid Strategies / Utility Dive: ~90 GW utility forecasts vs ~65 GW analyst view; duplicate-counting caveat

assertion: The North American Electric Reliability Corporation, which oversees grid reliability, found that 13 of 23 North American assessment areas face elevated or high risk of supply shortfalls within five years, with data centers as a main driver of load growth.
independent_value: NERC LTRA via POWER: 13 of 23

assertion: PJM's 2028/2029 auction cleared only 525 megawatts of new generation and plant upgrades
independent_value: PJM release: 525 MW of new generation and uprates

assertion: despite a record price
inaccuracy: The claim says the 2028/2029 auction had a record price; PJM says it cleared at $325, 2.5% below the prior auction's $333.44 cap, and the warehouse shows 2026/27 at $329.17.
sql: SELECT delivery_year, resource_clearing_price FROM energy.pjm_capacity_auction_prices WHERE lda='RTO' AND delivery_year>=2024
independent_value: PJM release: $325 vs prior $333.44 (-2.5%)

assertion: GE Vernova alone reported 116 gigawatts of gas turbine orders and reservations in mid-2026.
independent_value: Utility Dive: backlog 116 GW

assertion: In PJM, natural gas plants produced about 44% of the region's electricity in 2024, so gas prices weigh heavily on wholesale power prices.
independent_value: PJM 2024 State of the Market

assertion: The Henry Hub natural gas spot price set an all-time daily record of about $30.57 per million British thermal units on Jan. 26.
inaccuracy: The claim says $30.57 on Jan. 26; EIA's daily series shows $30.72 on Jan. 23 and $25.01 on Jan. 26, so $30.57 is NGI's averaged figure and the record date differs by source.
sql: SELECT report_date, value_dollars_per_mmbtu FROM energy.eia_natural_gas_price WHERE report_date BETWEEN '2026-01-22' AND '2026-01-30'

assertion: Day-ahead power prices at PJM's Western Hub cleared at $2,323 per megawatt-hour the next day.
reason: CBRE's cited PDF and S&P Global returned 403 to the engine; a web search shows CBRE citing $2,323/MWh day-ahead without naming a hub, and S&P reporting West Hub on-peak day-ahead for Jan. 27 at $890.01. The Western Hub attribution could not be confirmed.
why_no_page: CBRE (cited PDF and insights page) and S&P Global returned HTTP 403 to the engine fetch; the PJM market monitor Fern PDF was not opened.

assertion: The U.S. Department of Energy issued an emergency order allowing PJM to direct data centers and other large facilities onto backup generation as a last resort to prevent blackouts.
independent_value: DOE Section 202(c) Order No. 202-26-06

assertion: Ohio regulators approved a tariff in July 2025 requiring new AEP Ohio data centers above 25 megawatts to pay for at least 85% of their subscribed capacity for up to 12 years, regardless of actual use. Virginia regulators created a new rate class for Dominion Energy customers requiring 25 megawatts or more, effective in 2027. Oregon's 2025 law created a separate class for data centers above 20 megawatts, and Georgia now requires the state commission to review Georgia Power's large-load contracts.
independent_value: POWER, Cardinal News, Oregon PUC (Schedule 96, 20 MW)

assertion: The Data Center Coalition, an industry group, has called some of Oregon's rules out of step with other states.
independent_value: Fox Business: DCC told it the PUC order is 'significantly out of step with the approaches and best practices being implemented in many other states.'
